This guide is designed to clear up all the confusion. 1️⃣ The form must be filled out using the Latin alphabet. The...
html:
The Czech Republic long-term visa application form is one of the documents that students most often get stuck on and make mistakes with. The most frequently asked questions are: "How do I fill out the form, how should each section be written, is the Latin alphabet mandatory, are Turkish characters acceptable, and where should I sign?"

This guide is designed to clear up all the confusion.

1️⃣ The form must be filled out using the Latin alphabet.

The Czech Consulate only allows the form to be filled out using Latin characters. Therefore, Turkish characters should not be used.

✔ Correct spelling examples.

  • Şişli → SISLI

  • Cankaya → CANKAYA

  • Göktaş → GOKTAS

It's important to write the name exactly as it appears in the passport, but even if your passport contains Turkish characters, you should write the Latin equivalent on the form.

2️⃣ Filling out the form on a computer is the most accurate method.

Although the consulate accepts manual completion, the most secure method is to fill out the PDF form on a computer . This method...

  • It is more legible.

  • Reduces the risk of errors.

  • Deleting the document will not corrupt it.

Handwritten forms often have legibility issues.

3️⃣ Stapling Prohibited. Forms must not be stapled.

This topic has been frequently discussed in student chats. Application forms should absolutely not be stapled.

✔ The correct method.

  • Secure with a paperclip from the top.

  • Present it in the file if necessary.

If you use a staple, the document may be treated as "processed paper" in some places.

4️⃣ Color print is not required. Black and white is acceptable.

The consulate does not require color printouts. Black and white printouts are perfectly acceptable.

✔ Prevents unnecessary expenses

Most students are wasting money on color printouts.

5️⃣ The signature is placed on the last page. Not every page of the form is signed.

At the end of the form, there is a "Applicant's Signature" section. Only this section should be signed. Signing every page is considered a mistake.

✔ Suggestion

Use the same signature as in your passport.

6️⃣ The Most Confused Areas and Correct Answers

✔ “Place of Submission”

Enter the city you applied from → ISTANBUL / ANKARA

✔ “Purpose of Stay”

STUDY (Long-term)

✔ “Host Institution”

The English name of the university you were accepted to is written here.

✔ “Means of Financial Support”

GRANT + OWN FUNDS (If there is an Erasmus grant, this should be written)

✔ “Accommodation”

The address on the accommodation document must be written exactly as it appears.

✔ “Duration of Stay”

The dates must be exactly the same as those in the acceptance letter.

7️⃣ Using the Correct Form is Very Important

A common mistake mentioned in conversations: some students download and fill out tourist visa forms . This will definitely lead to rejection.

✔ Correct form.

"Long-term Visa Application Form – Czech Republic" (Usually 3 pages long)

8️⃣ Logical consistency is sought in the form.

The consulate wants the form not just to be filled out, but to make sense .

Example.

  • The accommodation start date and arrival date must be the same.

  • The length of stay and the duration of the grant should be compatible.

  • The passport must be valid for a sufficient period.

🎯 In short

Although the Czech Republic long-term application form may seem complex, it only takes 10 minutes if completed correctly. Key points:

  • Using Latin letters

  • Not stapling the form

  • Writing the correct dates

  • Just sign the last page.

If this process is done correctly, the most critical part of the application will be easily completed.

title: 🌍 Student Societies Comparison: IC Firenze, ESN, and AEGEE – Which One Is Right for You?
excerpt: Öğrenci Toplulukları Kıyaslaması: IC Firenze, ESN ve AEGEE Going abroad with Erasmus or an international exchange program is one of the most exciting experiences of your life. However, adapting to a new country and culture, making friends, and exploring all the opportunities the city has to offer can sometimes be challenging. That's where student clubs come in! There are many different student organizations on the market. In this article, we will compare a local organization like IC Firenze...
html:
Going abroad with Erasmus or an international exchange program is one of the most exciting experiences of your life. However, adapting to a new country and culture, making friends, and exploring all the opportunities the city has to offer can sometimes be challenging. That's where student clubs come in!

There are many different student organizations on the market. In this article, we will compare a local organization like IC Firenze with well-known European networks such as ESN (Erasmus Student Network) and AEGEE (Association des États Généraux des Étudiants de l'Europe) . Which one best suits your needs?

1. IC Firenze (International Community Florence)

We provided detailed information about IC Firenze in our previous article, but let's review its basic features for comparison:

  • Focus: A local organization, entirely focused on Florence.

  • Mission: To make Florence one of the most attractive cities for international students and to support students throughout their lives in the city.

  • Structure: An apolitical, non-profit association operating on the principle of "student-to-student" assistance.

  • What they offer:

    • IC Card: Discounts at partner venues and advantageous participation in events in Florence.

    • Activities: Special excursions to Florence and its surroundings (Pisa, Siena), city parties, aperitivos, language exchange nights, cultural events.

    • Practical Support: Accommodation guidance, assistance with bureaucratic processes (Codice Fiscale, Permesso di Soggiorno), affordable Italian language courses.

  • Suitable for: Ideal for students visiting Florence who are looking for a vibrant, city-centric social life, and want to benefit from local support and discounts. It offers a more personal and boutique experience.

2. ESN (Erasmus Student Network)

ESN is one of the largest and best-known student organizations in Europe.

  • Focus: It has a large network with more than 500 local branches in over 40 countries across Europe.

  • Mission: To enrich the experiences of Erasmus and other international exchange students in Europe and to ensure their social and cultural integration.

  • Structure: An international, non-profit, volunteer-based network. Each university/city has its own local chapter (e.g., ESN Firenze, ESN Rome).

  • What they offer:

    • ESNcard: This card, valid throughout Europe, offers discounts on international travel (train, bus), accommodation (hostel), airlines, language courses, and local activities (for example, it has partnerships with Ryanair, Flixbus, and Hostelling International).

    • Events: Local branches organize parties, cultural trips, and social events in their respective cities. There are also larger events organized by ESN at national and international levels (e.g., national platforms, EuroTrips).

    • Mentorship Programs: Volunteer local students mentor newly arrived international students on adapting to the city and university.

    • Social Projects: They organize various social responsibility projects and thematic weeks (Health Week, Environment Week, etc.).

  • Suitable for: Ideal for students planning to travel to different cities and countries in Europe, who want to take advantage of international travel discounts, be part of a wide network, and not be limited to Florence.

3. AEGEE (Association des États Généraux des Étudiants de l'Europe)

AEGEE is a European-based organization focused on student integration and personal development, primarily through lobbying and project-based initiatives.

  • Focus: It has local branches in over 130 cities across more than 40 countries. It focuses on European youth and integration.

  • Its mission is to foster the personal development of young people, bring together students from across Europe, promote active citizenship, and contribute to European integration.

  • Structure: A non-profit, volunteer-based, and apolitical youth organization.

  • What they offer:

    • Summer Universities: One of AEGEE's best-known events. These are 1-2 week programs held in different European cities during the summer months, focusing on cultural, academic, or thematic topics. Participants receive training and also participate in social activities.

    • Conferences and Working Groups: They organize seminars, conferences, and working groups across Europe on topics such as youth policies, sustainability, and human rights.

    • Project Management and Lobbying: They work with the European Commission and other organizations to draw attention to the problems of young people and to influence policies.

    • Networking: Offers opportunities to meet young people from different cultures and build long-term international connections.

  • Suitable for: Ideal for students who want to invest in personal development, improve leadership skills, develop projects in areas such as politics, environment or human rights, and build broad international networks, going beyond just parties and trips. Conclusion: Which one should you choose?

Your choice depends entirely on your expectations and goals:

  • If you're only staying in Florence and want to explore the city thoroughly and make the most of what local has to offer, IC Firenze is a great starting point. You'll stay on top of the city's pulse with local discounts and Florence-focused events.

  • If you plan to travel extensively throughout Europe, meet people from different countries, and take advantage of discounts on your travels, you should definitely join ESN . Its wide network and the benefits of the ESNcard will make your Erasmus experience much more economical and enriching.

You will broaden your horizons with international conferences and Summer Universities.

title: IC Firenze (International Community Florence): Your Erasmus Guide in Florence

html:
If you're an Erasmus student embarking on a new adventure in the historic streets of Florence, one of the quickest ways to adapt to the city and its social life is to join student communities. IC Firenze (International Community Florence) , much like ESN (Erasmus Student Network) but entirely focused on Florence and a local, friendly community, can be your biggest support in this regard.

👥 What is IC Firenze? What exactly do they do?

IC Firenze is a non-profit, apolitical student association founded to support international students and Erasmus participants arriving in Florence. Its core principle is quite simple: student-to-student help. Volunteer students who have previously experienced similar situations help newcomers seamlessly adapt to the city, culture, and university life.

  • Local Focus: Unlike an international network like ESN, IC Firenze's entire energy and resources are dedicated to Florence. This allows them to offer a more boutique and focused experience, specific to the city.

  • Their mission: To make Florence one of the most attractive and livable cities for international students, and to support students from the process before their arrival in the city throughout their stay.

💳 The famous IC Card: Your Passport in Florence

One of IC Firenze's most popular services is the IC Card , a membership card. Typically available for around €15 , this card offers numerous benefits throughout the season.

What do you get with an IC Card?

  • Event Discounts: You get discounted or sometimes free access to all parties, trips, and events organized by IC Firenze.

  • Venue Deals: You'll receive exclusive discounts at participating bars, pubs (such as popular student hangouts like The Lion's Fountain), restaurants, and pizzerias.

  • Service Discounts: Special offers are available for services such as gyms, travel agencies, and even opening a bank account.

  • Free Drinks: Many parties and events offer cardholders a complimentary "welcome drink".

Is it worth it? If you're a social student and plan on attending at least one or two events a week, the card will easily pay for itself in the first few weeks.

🎉 More Than Just a Party: IC Firenze Event Calendar

IC Firenze has a very wide range of activities that cater to all types of students.

  1. Social and Cultural Activities:

    • Welcome Days/Party: The biggest get-together event at the beginning of the semester, bringing all the new students together.

    • Aperitivo Linguistico (Language Exchange Nights): Relaxed and social gatherings that bring together students who want to practice different languages. Great for improving your Italian!

    • Cultural Dinners: Delicious evenings where everyone brings a dish from their own country and explores world cuisines.

    • Themed Parties: Costume and themed parties for special occasions such as Halloween, Carnival, or end-of-term holidays.

  2. Excursions and Discovery Tours:

    • Day Trips: Bus tours to Tuscan gems such as Pisa, Siena, Cinque Terre, and San Gimignano.

    • Weekend Trips: Overnight trips to larger cities like Rome, Venice, or Milan.

    • Outdoor Activities: Hiking and trekking events organized in the magnificent hills of Tuscany.

🏠 From Accommodation to Bureaucracy: Practical Support

One of IC Firenze's most valuable services is the practical assistance it provides. This support can be a lifesaver, especially for a student arriving in Italy for the first time.

  • Accommodation Support: They provide guidance in finding reliable landlords and apartments. They warn you against rental scams.

  • Bureaucratic Assistance: They guide you through complex processes in Italy, such as obtaining a tax identification number ( Codice Fiscale ) or a residence permit ( Permesso di Soggiorno ), which every student must acquire.

  • Italian Language Courses: Through their partner language schools, they organize affordable Italian lessons for international students.

📞 How to Get There and Join the Community?

It is quite easy to contact IC Firenze and stay informed about their events.

  • Official Website: This should be your first stop for the latest information, event calendar, and card details.

  • Email Address: You can write directly for any questions, suggestions, and support requests.

    • info@erasmusfirenze.it

  • Social Media: Be sure to follow their social media accounts to avoid missing event announcements, photos, and instant updates. Instagram is especially their most active platform.

    • Instagram: @icfirenze

    • Facebook: International Community Firenze

Offices: You can visit their offices, which are usually active at the beginning of the term, to pick up your IC Card and get information in person. Check their website or social media announcements for office addresses and opening hours.

✅ Summary: Should you join IC Firenze?

Advantages:

  • In Florence, you instantly become part of a large and international social circle.

  • With IC Card, you can save a significant amount of money while living in the city.

  • Regular activities will leave you with no chance of getting bored.

  • You receive reliable support during challenging processes such as accommodation and bureaucracy.

Disadvantages:

  • It focuses solely on Florence; it is not part of an international network like ESN.

  • Popular tours can fill up quickly.

In conclusion, if you want to have a fulfilling, social, and hassle-free Erasmus or exchange program experience in Florence, joining the IC Firenze community is one of the best steps you can take. Your first task upon arriving in the city should be to find their "Welcome Day" event!

title: 📬 Czech Republic Erasmus Visa - Late Arrival of Accommodation Document - How Does the 30-Day Extension Work?

html:
The biggest concern for students applying for Erasmus in the Czech Republic is the delayed arrival of their accommodation documents. Paper documents, especially those sent via "Ceska Posta," can sometimes be delayed for weeks. Students frequently encounter this situation, thinking, "I think the post office lost the document; it won't arrive in time for my appointment, what will happen?"

This guide details the official extension period offered by the Czech Republic in case of a delayed accommodation document and the steps you need to follow.

1️⃣ The original accommodation document must be brought.

One of the most critical documents for long-term Czech visas is the "Accommodation Confirmation." This document is generally submitted in two formats.

  • 📄 Physical letter (stamped by Ceska Posta)

  • 📧 PDF preview (some universities send this, but it's not official)

The consulate does not accept PDF printouts as official documents in most cases. The original document is the stamped copy delivered by the postal service (PTT) .

2️⃣ What happens if PTT (Turkish Post Office) delays the delivery? The "Extra Time Right" comes into effect.

Students' biggest fear is not having enough documents for their appointment. However, the Czech Consulate has an official procedure to resolve this issue.

✔ Rule.

If your accommodation documents arrive late, the consulate may grant an additional 30 days .

So, not having the required documents at the appointment doesn't mean your application will be rejected. You can submit the documents later.

This information has been confirmed numerous times in group chats.

3️⃣ How Does the Additional Time Period Work? Step-by-Step Explanation

🟩 1. Attend your appointment – Report if you don't have the required documents.

Just tell the officer, "The document is delayed at the post office."

🟩 2. The officer will give you a form for missing documents.

This form indicates which documents are missing .

🟩 3. They will grant the additional time in writing.

Additional time is generally granted.

  • 15 days

  • 30 days. It varies depending on the situation, but most students are given 30 days .

🟩 4. You will submit the document to the consulate later when it arrives.

You don't need to re-enter the appointment.

4️⃣ Why is the “Blue Ceska Postal Stamp” on the Back of the Accommodation Document Important?

An interesting detail for students: There's a blue stamp on the back of the document. This stamp indicates the document's authenticity.

✔ The consulate performs the following checks.

  • The document must have a wet signature.

  • Presence of the institution's seal.

  • The appearance of the blue postage stamp.

PDF printouts are not considered official because they do not contain this stamp.

5️⃣ PDF is for “Temporary Viewing” Only

Some universities send the document both physically and as a PDF. Students print out the PDF and bring it with them, but the consulate often considers it only a preliminary document .

✔ PDF can be used for the following:

  • Preparing for the appointment

  • To be submitted as a temporary document for course registration.

  • University pre-registration procedures

But it is not sufficient on its own for a visa .

6️⃣ What should you do if the document gets lost on the way?

This happens more often than you think. Even if PTT or Ceska Posta doesn't report it lost, the document may not appear in the system.

✔ Solution.

  1. Email the university's international office.

  2. Request the document to be resent.

  3. If possible, ask them to use DHL or UPS.

  4. Inform the consulate.

The consulate will wait for the document – it will not reject the application.

7️⃣ Late Document Submission Does Not Affect Visa Approval

The consulate requires all documents to be submitted in a complete file. Even if the accommodation document arrives late, the process will be completed with the same speed.

✔ So.

Late submission does not equal delayed evaluation. The process will continue once this document is added to the file.

🎯 RESULTS

Late arrival of accommodation documents is one of the most common problems with Czech Republic Erasmus applications. However, the consulate is aware of this and grants students an official 30-day extension. Therefore, going to the appointment without the document is not a problem. Simply submit it when it arrives. The original copy with the blue Ceska postal stamp is the most critical part of the application.

title: Italy DSU Toscana Scholarship Amounts
excerpt: DSU Toscana Burs Miktarları The scholarship amount is determined based on the ISEE document, which shows the student's economic situation, and three main criteria: Cash Scholarship (Quota Monetaria) The official scholarship announcement for 2025/2026 (band) does not yet include exact figures in tabular form for these categories. However, since increases are made each year in line with the previous year's figures, the official maximum amounts for the 2024/2025 academic year are the most...
html:
The scholarship amount is determined based on the ISEE document, which shows the student's economic situation, and three main criteria:

  1. Cash Scholarship (Quota Monetaria)

    The official scholarship announcement for 2025/2026 (band) does not yet include exact figures in tabular form for these categories. However, since increases are made each year in line with the previous year's figures, the official maximum amounts for the 2024/2025 academic year are the most reliable source of reference .

    • Fuori Sede (Student Studying in a City Different from Their Place of Residence):

      • Maximum Annual Scholarship: €6,656

      • This group receives the highest payment because their accommodation and living expenses are higher.

    • Pendolare (Student whose residence and school are in different municipalities and who provides transportation):

      • Maximum Annual Scholarship: €3,598

      • This category includes students who attend school every day but do not live with their families.

    • In Sede (Students Living in the Same City as Their School or with Their Family):

      • Maximum Annual Scholarship: €2,682

      • The lowest level of cash support is given to this group.

    ⚠️ Important Note: These figures are gross amounts. If the student uses dormitory and cafeteria services, the cost of these services will be deducted from the total scholarship amount, and the remaining amount will be paid in cash.

  2. In-kind support (Services replacing cash)

    • Meal Support: University cafeterias (mensa) provide the right to one or two free or very low-cost meals a day. This translates to savings of hundreds of euros annually.

    • Accommodation Support (Dormitory): Students who are awarded dormitory accommodation through the scholarship application process do not pay any extra fees for accommodation. The cost of dormitory services is deducted from the cash scholarship amount mentioned above.

  3. Rent Support (Contributo Affitto)

    This is a cash rent assistance program for students with fuori sede status who did not qualify for dormitory accommodation. The finalized figures for the 2025/2026 academic year are as follows:

    • Annual Rent Contribution: €3,000

    • Semi-Annual (Single Term) Contribution: €1,500

⏰ Payment Schedule and Frequent Delays

Scholarship payments are usually made in two installments:

  • 1st Installment (50%): During the Autumn/Winter months (usually November–December is targeted).

  • 2nd Installment (50%): During the spring semester (usually March-April).

⚠️ Student Experience: Delays of up to 3-4 months, especially in the payment of the first installment, are quite common. This can cause significant financial difficulties for new students arriving in Italy during their first few months. Therefore, it is vital to plan a budget to cover the first few months before arriving, relying on scholarship payments.

💡 Problems Students Face and Practical Tips

  1. "Why is the scholarship amount less than expected?"

    • The problem: The biggest confusion for students is that the entire announced maximum amount is not received in cash.

    • Solution: Remember that the value of free meals and (if applicable) dorm services will be deducted from your total scholarship amount. The net cash you receive will depend on how much you utilize these services.

  2. "Rent Support is Insufficient"

    • The problem: In large, touristy cities like Florence, Pisa, and Siena, average room rents are around €500-700 per month. The annual rent subsidy of €3,000 is insufficient to cover these costs.

    • Tip: View rent assistance as part of your budget, not the whole thing. When looking for a home, consider more affordable suburban areas or larger shared apartments.

  3. "I can't get clear information from the DSU office."

    • Problem: DSU offices can be busy and email responses may be delayed. Websites may not always reflect the most up-to-date information.

    • Tip: Contact the relevant department directly to get exact figures specific to your case.

      • Telephone: Call 055 2347200 and ask for the "Servizio Benefici e Interventi Monetari" (Cash Assistance and Payments Service) unit.

      • Email: Request a written net amount to be applied to you by sending an email to urp@dsu.toscana.it stating your status (fuori sede/pendolare/in sede) and your ISEE value.

One of the biggest problems for students going to the Czech Republic for Erasmus is choosing the right phone line and internet package . Students who activate roaming with their Turkish phone lines experience a bill shock within minutes. “The daily fee has gone up to 250 TL, never use it!” This blog analyzes all the experiences in student conversations and explains step-by-step the cheapest, fastest, and most sensible phone line options in the Czech Republic.

1️⃣ Why Using a Turkish Phone Line is Illogical

Most students try to activate their Turkish SIM card and use the internet during the first few days. However, roaming charges in the Czech Republic are quite high.

✔ Average roaming costs.

  • Vodafone. ~250 TL per day.

  • Turkcell. ~279 TL per day.

  • Turk Telekom. The non-application package is much more expensive.

Therefore, using the internet with a Turkish network is definitely not sensible .

Türkiye line only.

  • Receiving SMS

  • Simply keeping it open is enough for bank verification.

2️⃣ The Cheapest and Most Recommended Phone Line by Students in the Czech Republic: Tesco Mobile

Tesco Mobile is the cheapest mobile phone line recommended by 80% of students. It's both affordable and offers a wide range of packages.

✔ Popular student package.

299 CZK → 20 GB + 30 GB (Approximately 50 GB total)

The advantages of this package.

  • Affordable price

  • Most parts of the Czech Republic have good reception.

  • Student-friendly promotions

  • Easy activation with ID.

3️⃣ Other Popular Operators

Besides Tesco Mobile, there are three other major operators. However, their prices are higher than student packages.

📌 Vodafone Czech Republic

  • High-speed internet within Europe

  • High shooting quality.

  • The price is higher. It is usually preferred by local students.

📌 T-Mobile CZ

  • Wide coverage area

  • Short-term packages are available.

  • Good value for money.

📌 O2 Czech Republic

  • Prices are moderate.

  • New line activation is easy.

None of these are as economical as Tesco.

4️⃣ The Most Sensible Settings for Students Using Dual SIM Cards

Most students participating in the Erasmus program use dual-SIM phones. This setup prevents line interference and resolves noise issues.

✔ The best way to use it.

  • Turkish line. Only calls and SMS should be enabled.

  • Czech Republic network. All internet and mobile data active.

  • Set up the data SIM card manually using the checkbox.

  • Turn off roaming settings.

This way you won't experience bill shock and there won't be internet outages.

5️⃣ Where to buy a SIM card?

It is most easily obtained from the following points.

  • Tesco supermarkets

  • O2 stores

  • Mobile operator kiosks

  • Mobile hotline stand at the airport

  • University orientation day stands

✔ Recommendation

Buying them at the airport is expensive . It's more convenient to buy them from a supermarket when you arrive in the city.

6️⃣ Documents Required for Line Activation

✔ That's all you need.

  • Passport

No additional documents are required from the student. It will be activated immediately.

7️⃣ What is the mobile internet quality like in the Czech Republic?

Czech Republic is one of the most stable countries in Europe in terms of mobile internet.

✔ Average speeds.

  • Download speed: 40–80 Mbps

  • Upload speed: 10–20 Mbps

There are fewer disruptions on campuses, tram lines, and in urban areas.

8️⃣ The Most Suitable Packages for Short-Term Visits

If you're only staying for a few weeks, this package is suitable.

  • Tesco Mobile 100–150 CZK mini pack

  • 5–10 GB internet. This package is recommended for students for short-term stays.

🎯 In short

In the Czech Republic, the most advantageous mobile plan is Tesco Mobile . It offers around 50 GB of internet for a low price of 299 CZK, making it perfect for students. Leaving your Turkish SIM card active only for SMS verification will save you money. If you configure the dual SIM settings correctly, both internet and calls will be secure.

This guide summarizes the most up-to-date phone line and internet packages for Erasmus students in 2025.

title: 🎤 Czech Republic Erasmus Visa. Is there an interview? What languages are spoken?
excerpt: One of the most frequently asked questions by Czech Erasmus students is, "Is there an interview, what kind of questions are asked, is it in English, is it difficult?" There is NO interview for Erasmus in the Czech Republic. The process is entirely based on document submission. In this blog, based on real student testimonials, I've explained step-by-step how the Erasmus long-term visa process works and clarified all the misconceptions surrounding the interview. 1️⃣ There are absolutely no...
html:
One of the most frequently asked questions by Czech Erasmus students is, "Is there an interview, what kind of questions are asked, is it in English, is it difficult?" There is NO interview for Erasmus in the Czech Republic. The process is entirely based on document submission.

In this blog, based on real student testimonials, I've explained step-by-step how the Erasmus long-term visa process works and clarified all the misconceptions surrounding the interview.

1️⃣ There are absolutely no interviews in Istanbul.

Most of the students applying are from Istanbul, and they all say the same thing: "The officer was Turkish, but he didn't conduct the interview."

✔ The process in Istanbul.

  • You're coming in

  • You are taking a number.

  • You are submitting the documents.

  • The staff member reports if there are any missing items.

  • You give your fingerprints.

  • You're going out

There are no questions or oral interviews at any stage.

2️⃣ No interviews are conducted in Ankara either.

Even though Ankara is a more meticulous center, there is no interview process .

Officer.

  • He checks the documents.

  • It scans your file.

  • He/She takes his/her passport

  • It takes fingerprints.

No oral interview will be conducted.

3️⃣ Why are there no interviews? Czech Republic has a different system.

Unlike other European countries, the Czech Republic does not require oral interviews for long-term visas . Here's why.

  • All decisions are made by the Czech Ministry of Internal Affairs.

  • The consulate is merely a document submission center.

  • The evaluation is based entirely on the submitted files.

Therefore, there is no need to speak with the applicant.

4️⃣ Only one question can be asked: “You have missing documents.”

Sometimes the officer may ask a few questions to point out any missing documents. This is not an interview .

Example.

  • "Where is the original of this document?"

  • "This document lacks an apostille."

  • "Will your accommodation document arrive later?"

This is a purely technical discussion.

5️⃣ Language Issue: No English or Czech is spoken.

Throughout the process.

  • No questions are asked in English.

  • Czech is not accepted for communication.

  • You won't be interviewed.

Everything proceeds with the assistance of a Turkish-speaking officer .

✔ In short.

No interview + no foreign language requirement + no questions.

6️⃣ Outdated Information That Confuses Students

Some blogs contain this information from years ago: "Czech citizens may conduct interviews."

This information is very old and outdated. Current practice is that there are no interviews for long-term Erasmus visas.

7️⃣ Even without an interview, great attention is paid to the documents.

Although the absence of interviews simplifies the process, the Czech Republic is known for its rigorous documentation .

The most closely watched documents.

  • Accommodation document

  • Financial adequacy

  • Criminal record

  • Application form

  • Passport validity period

If the documents are correct, the process will proceed smoothly.

🎯 In short

For the Czech Republic Erasmus long-term visa, there is no interview , and the entire process involves simply submitting documents to a Turkish-speaking officer. No questions are asked in English or Czech. All you need to do before going to the consulate is ensure your documents are complete.

Therefore, the Czech Republic is one of the smoothest countries for students who are afraid of interviews.

html:
One of the most critical points in the Romanian student visa process is choosing the correct consulate.The appointment location is determined not by the city where the student studies. but strictly by the official residence address.This rule never changes and is evaluated only through the residence certificate.

This guide explains Romania’s consular jurisdictions. which province belongs to which center. and how to choose the correct appointment location.

1️⃣ Romania Accepts Long-Term Visa Applications Through Three Centers in Turkey

Long-term Romanian visa applications are processed in three main offices:

✔ Istanbul Consulate GeneralCovers most of the Marmara and Black Sea region.

✔ Ankara EmbassyHas the widest jurisdiction in Turkey.

✔ Izmir ConsulateAccepts applications from selected Aegean provinces.

Each applicant must apply only through the center responsible for their residence province.

2️⃣ The Residence Rule Is Absolute. The Student’s University Address Does NOT Count

The only determining factor is the province where your official residence is registered.The city where you study or temporarily live has no influence on your appointment location.

Examples.A student studying in Antalya but with residence in Samsun applies through Istanbul.A student studying in Ankara but officially residing in Izmir applies through Izmir.A student studying in Bursa but registered in Ankara applies through Ankara.

This rule is never flexible.

3️⃣ Updated Province Distribution. Which City Belongs to Which Center?

The lists below follow the official consular jurisdiction of Romania.

🟦 Provinces Under the Istanbul Consulate General

Marmara Region

IstanbulKocaeliSakaryaYalovaBursaBalıkesirÇanakkaleTekirdağEdirneKırklareli

Black Sea Region

ZonguldakBartınKarabükDüzceSamsunSinopOrduGiresunTrabzonRizeArtvin

📌 Anyone residing in these provinces must make their appointment through Istanbul.

🟥 Provinces Under the Ankara Embassy

Central Anatolia

AnkaraKonyaEskişehirKayseriSivasYozgatKırıkkaleKırşehirAksarayNiğdeNevşehirÇankırı

Eastern & Southeastern Anatolia

ErzurumElazığMalatyaGaziantepDiyarbakırŞanlıurfaMardinBatmanBitlisSiirtŞırnakHakkariVanAğrıKarsIğdırArdahanMuşTunceli

Mediterranean (selected provinces)

AdanaMersinHatayOsmaniye

📌 This center covers the highest number of applicants nationwide.

🟩 Provinces Under the Izmir Consulate

Aegean Region

IzmirManisaAydınMuğlaDenizliKütahyaUşak

📌 All residents of these provinces submit their applications through Izmir.

4️⃣ Can You Change Your Appointment Center by Changing Your Residence?

Yes. but only under certain conditions.

The residence change must:

✔ Be registered at the Population Directorate✔ Appear updated on e-Devlet✔ Match the address written on your visa application form

Otherwise. the consulate will not accept your application.

5️⃣ How Should the Address Be Written on Forms?

If the address is inconsistent. the application may be invalid.

Correct format:

• Neighborhood• Street or Avenue• Building number• Apartment number• District• City

No abbreviations should be used.

6️⃣ Which Center Is Faster?

General processing tendencies:

✔ IstanbulMore staff. high volume but steady workflow.

✔ AnkaraDocuments examined in detail. sometimes slightly slower.

✔ IzmirLower application numbers. generally smooth process.

There is no guaranteed duration. each file is individually reviewed.

🎯 Summary

Choosing the correct consulate is one of the most critical steps in the Romanian student visa process.Your appointment must be booked through the center responsible for your official residence.Your address must be consistent across all documents.

This guide clearly shows the consular distribution for each province and helps ensure a correct application.sürecini doğru şekilde planlamanı sağlar.

html:
The Romanian Erasmus visa application process has become a well-organized and rigorous procedure.

Applicants are particularly interested in the latest regulations regarding document uploading systems, appointment locations, and financial eligibility.

This guide explains the Romanian Erasmus visa application process for 2026 step-by-step in a modern and understandable way.

1️⃣ Type of Erasmus Visa for Romania in 2026

The visa obtained by Erasmus students in Romania is: Visa D – Long Stay for Studies (Student Mobility)

This visa is generally based on the 2026 academic calendar.

  • 120 days

  • 180 days

  • It is issued for a period of 1 year.

2️⃣ 2026 Appointment System. Application Centers and Regional Requirements.

Romania's appointment system will operate entirely on a regional basis in 2026. The biggest mistake students make is making appointments with the wrong consulate .

✔ Istanbul Consulate General

Large parts of the Marmara and Black Sea regions.

✔ Ankara Embassy

Central Anatolia, Eastern Anatolia, Southeastern Anatolia.

✔ Izmir Consulate

Some provinces in the Aegean Region. Some provinces may be redirected to Ankara again.

The rule hasn't changed. You must make your appointment at the center associated with your residential address .

3️⃣ Updated Document List for Romania Erasmus Visa 2026

Romania has tightened document controls for 2026. The following documents are now required as standard.

📄 1. Long-Term Visa Application Form

It is completed and signed online.

📁 2nd Passport

A minimum validity of 1 year is recommended. Bringing your old passports is also helpful.

🏫 3. University Acceptance Letter

It must be signed and stamped. A PDF is not sufficient; a printed copy must be submitted.

📚 4. Learning Agreement (2026 Format)

It must be signed by three people, with clear dates written on it.

🏠 5. Accommodation Document

University dorm, private accommodation, or contract. Some schools integrate accommodation information into the letter.

💶 6. Bank Statement (Amount Updated as of 2026)

Romania has increased its financial sufficiency targets for 2026.

✔ New minimum amount.

Minimum monthly cost €650 × duration of stay

Example.

  • Student staying for 5 months → €3250

  • Student staying for 6 months → €3900

Turkish lira accounts are accepted, but the statement must be clear.

👤 7. Sponsorship Letter (Optional)

Family support is added if needed. Notarization provides extra security, but it is not mandatory.

🩺 8. Health Insurance (2026 Coverage Update)

Minimum security deposit for a Romanian residence permit in 2026: €40,000.

The insurance must be valid throughout the entire Schengen area.

👮 9. Criminal Record

The English version of the e-government system is accepted. An apostille is still required at some centers; it's helpful to include it.

🛫 10. Flight Ticket (Optional)

It is not mandatory. It is recommended to obtain it after the visa has been approved.

4️⃣ Tighter Regulations in 2026: What Has Changed?

The Romanian Ministry of Interior is placing greater emphasis on certain aspects regarding student visas for 2026.

✔ The student's financial sufficiency should be clearly visible.

Account transactions should not be suspicious.

✔ Accommodation document must be genuine.

If forged letters of guarantee are detected, the application will be rejected.

✔ LA dates and visa form must match.

Date discrepancies frequently cause delays.

✔ The insurance period must fully cover the Erasmus duration.

The case may be suspended if too many days are left unattended.

5️⃣ Step-by-Step Process for Appointment Day 2026

1. Document verification is performed.

The deficiencies will be pointed out, and you may be given a period of time to complete them.

2. Fingerprints are taken.

It is mandatory for all long-term visas.

3. Passport is returned.

Sometimes it may be returned to the applicant and requested again once a decision is made.

4. Average processing time

20–50 days . In some cities, this period may be even shorter.

6️⃣ 2026 Financial Adequacy Logic

Romania requires students to have both an Erasmus grant and personal savings.

✔ If there is a grant

The total amount of the grant will be included in the bank statement. The remaining amount must be covered by the student or sponsor.

✔ No grant available

The full amount must be in the account.

7️⃣ Insurance Updates for 2026

In 2026, some insurance policies were not accepted for Romanian residence permits. Therefore, there are things to consider when choosing insurance.

✔ Correct guarantee

€40,000 minimum (€45,000 recommended for the full year)

✔ Coverage area

It must state that it is valid in all Schengen countries.

8️⃣ Common Mistakes Students Will Make in 2026

  • Uploading accommodation documents late

  • Getting insurance with low coverage.

  • Submit an old bank statement.

  • Missing signature on the learning agreement

  • Booking an appointment at the wrong consulate.

  • Buying unnecessary plane tickets while waiting

These errors cause delays in the application process.

🎯 In short

The most critical points for obtaining a Romanian Erasmus visa in 2026 are: Making an appointment with the correct consulate; clearly demonstrating financial sufficiency; submitting accommodation documents on time; arranging health insurance with coverage valid until 2026; and submitting all documents completely and in the correct format.

When these conditions are met, the Romanian Erasmus visa will be approved without any problems.

html:
For Czech Erasmus students, the most stressful period is waiting for an answer to the question "What is the status of your application?" after submitting it. The mysterious statuses on the Czech Ministry of Internal Affairs website, in particular, confuse students. "Application received," "Assessment," "Pending," "Completed." What do these expressions mean, and which are good and which are bad?

In this blog, I explain all the steps in a simple and clear way.

1️⃣ Where can I check the system status?

Czech Republic long-term visa application status can be checked at this address: 👉 Ministry of Interior (MOI) Visa Application Tracking

Three pieces of information are required for the search.

  • Passport number

  • Date of birth

  • Application type

The inquiry screen displays the result in two seconds.

2️⃣ When will the application be submitted to the system?

This is the point that students get confused about the most. The system is not updated immediately after the application.

✔ Average times.

  • Forwarding from the consulate to the Ministry of Interior. 5-10 days.

  • The file will be processed. 10-20 days.

  • It will appear in the system in 20-30 days.

So the application won't be visible immediately, which is perfectly normal.

3️⃣ Explanation of All Statuses Seen in the System

Now let's move on to the most critical part. I will explain each and every phrase that appears in the system.

🟩 1. “Application Received”

This means your application has been received by the system. No action has been taken yet, but the document has reached the Czech Republic.

This is a good sign.

🟩 2. “In Process” or “Assessment”

It is the longest stage.

At this stage.

  • The documents are checked.

  • Accommodation is confirmed.

  • Financial adequacy is examined.

  • A security and intelligence screening is conducted.

  • Your university acceptance is confirmed.

The average processing time is 30–90 days . For some applications, it may take up to 120 days .

🟩 3. “Additional Review” or “Pending Documents”

This indicates that there is additional processing required for one of the documents.

Example.

  • Accommodation confirmation

  • Financial control

  • Document readability

The consulate may call you, but most of the time you'll just be asked to wait.

🟩 4. “Processing Completed”

This statement represents the stage where students are happiest.

This indicates that the evaluation is complete . However, a decision may not yet have been announced.

The consulate usually sends an email 1-5 days later. It's most likely confirmation.

🟩 5. “Issued / Approved”

Your visa has been approved. From this moment on, the consulate will begin preparing your passport.

🟥 6. “Rejected / Not Approved”

This is a rare occurrence. In this case, the consulate sends an official decision letter.

4️⃣ Why is the status not updating in the system?

Students often ask, "It's been writing the same thing for a month, is there a problem?"

No. The system updates very slowly.

✔ Reasons for update delays.

  • The files are processed manually.

  • Security checks take a long time.

  • There may be public holidays or high traffic.

  • The inquiry system is not updated for weeks.

Even if the situation doesn't change, the process continues.

5️⃣ What does it mean if the inquiry screen is blank?

This is the most panic-inducing situation: "It looked like my application wasn't there."

This usually happens for the following reasons.

  • The file has not yet been uploaded to the system.

  • The system is undergoing maintenance.

  • Your internet browser is not displaying the page due to a cookie issue.

That doesn't mean there were no applications.

6️⃣ The Healthiest Monitoring Method

✔ Check once a week

Checking it every day creates stress and doesn't strain the system.

✔ Pay attention to emails from the consulate.

The decision usually comes via email.

✔ Don't lose contact with your university.

In some cases, the school expedites the accommodation confirmation process.

🎯 In short

Although the Czech Ministry of Internal Affairs' tracking system might seem like a challenging process for students, it's actually very simple. Status updates are slow, but the process constantly progresses. The most critical stage is the "Assessment" phase, and patience is required. Once the system is updated, a decision is usually announced within a few days.

html:
Students who go to Romania for long-term education are required to have health insurance. This is especially important for Erasmus students because if the policy is incorrect. the visa may be delayed and additional costs may arise during the Romanian residence permit stage.

This guide explains all essential information step by step.

1️⃣ Which Health Insurance Does Romania Accept?

For the long-term student visa. Romania requires a travel health insurance that meets specific conditions.

Mandatory Coverage

✔️ Minimum 30.000 euro coverage✔️ Valid in all Schengen countries✔️ Must cover the entire study period✔️ Must include emergency treatment. hospitalization and medical repatriation

These requirements are checked again during the residence permit application.

2️⃣ How Should the Insurance Duration Be?

The policy dates are extremely important. It must meet these conditions.

✔️ Start before the beginning of the study period✔️ Continue beyond the end of the semester✔️ Must not conflict with the Learning Agreement

If the study period is 5 months. the policy should cover 5 months + a safety margin.

3️⃣ Which Insurance Companies Are Suitable?

Many students choose companies offering wide coverage.

Commonly Preferred Companies

AllianzAxaGulfGeneraliMapfre

The brand is not important. what matters is that the policy meets Romanian requirements.

4️⃣ Additional Requirements for the Residence Permit

Yes. after entering Romania with a visa. students must apply for a residence permit. Extra checks may occur.

Possible Additional Conditions

✔️ Policy must cover the remaining full study period✔️ Insurance certificate must be in English or Romanian✔️ Emergency and hospitalization coverage must be clearly stated

Students with low-coverage policies may be required to purchase a new insurance during residence procedures.

5️⃣ Most Common Mistakes

Many visa applications fail due to incorrect insurance.

🚫 1. Buying a cheap policy with low coverageThis delays the visa or leads to residence rejection.

🚫 2. Choosing a policy shorter than the Erasmus periodIf Erasmus is 5 months but the policy is 90 days. the application is invalid.

🚫 3. Policy valid only for departure from TurkeyIt must be valid in the entire Schengen area.

🚫 4. Name mismatch between passport and insuranceBoth must match exactly.

🚫 5. Submitting a simple screenshot of the policyConsulates require a PDF with stamp and signature.

6️⃣ How to Add the Insurance to the Visa File?

✔️ Submit a color printout✔️ Include all pages of the policy✔️ Coverage amount must be visible✔️ Coverage region must be specified✔️ Signature and stamp section must be clear

Submitting only the summary counts as missing documents.

7️⃣ Link Between Insurance and Bank Statement

In Romanian student visa applications. financial proof and insurance are evaluated together.

✔️ The more comprehensive the insurance is✔️ The clearer the required bank balance becomes

Weak insurance means stricter financial review.

🎯 Summary

Health insurance is one of the most important elements of a Romanian student visa.

⭐ Coverage must be at least 30.000 euro⭐ Must be valid in the entire Schengen zone⭐ Must cover the full study period⭐ Must be submitted in professional format

A properly prepared insurance policy becomes one of the strongest parts of the application.

html:
Romania Student Visa Guide. The Most Important Part Is Showing Financial Sufficiency Correctly

For Romania, the financial section is the most sensitive part of the student visa. Almost all documents are accepted without issues.However, bank statements, account activity and sponsor letters are where the most mistakes occur.

This guide explains in full detail how students should present their financial situation when applying for a Romanian visa.

1️⃣ How Much Money Should Be in the Bank Account for a Romanian Student Visa?

Romania wants to be sure that the student can support their living expenses.For this reason, a certain minimum amount must appear in the bank account.

Minimum Balance Principle

Basic calculation:

Monthly living cost × duration of stay = minimum required amount

The widely accepted monthly amount is €500–€650.

Examples:

• For 5 months → €2500–€3250• For 6 months → €3000–€3900• For 10 months → €5000–€6500

This amount can also be shown in local currency.A euro account is not mandatory.

2️⃣ How Should the Bank Statement Look?

Romania places great importance on the bank statement. It must meet the following requirements:

✔ Must have a wet signature from the bankScreenshots from e-government or mobile banking are not accepted.

✔ Account activity must be clean and consistentSudden large deposits appear suspicious.

✔ Last 3 months of transactions must be included

✔ If the balance is in local currency, the embassy will convert it using the daily exchange rate

✔ The account must belong to the studentIf it belongs to a family member, a sponsor letter becomes mandatory.

3️⃣ How Should Students Receiving Erasmus Grants Show Their Finances?

Erasmus grants support financial sufficiency, but the grant letter alone is not enough.

✔ Grant letter must be included in the file✔ Grant + bank balance must complement each otherExample, if the grant is €1500 and the stay is 5 months, the remaining €1000–€1500 must be shown in the bank account.✔ It doesn’t matter if the grant hasn’t been paid yet — the document proves the upcoming payment.

4️⃣ Is a Sponsor Letter Mandatory?

A sponsor letter is not always required, but it becomes necessary in the following cases:

• Insufficient balance in the student’s account• Money located in a family member’s account• The student has no regular income• Account activity does not belong to the student

Typical sponsors:

• Mother• Father• Legal guardian

A sponsor letter should include:

• Sponsor’s personal details• Relationship to the student• Duration of financial support• Support commitment• Signature• Sponsor’s own bank statement attached

Notary approval is optional but adds credibility.

5️⃣ How to Show Money Stored in a Family Account?

A family account alone is not accepted.The embassy assumes the money does not belong to the student.

Therefore these three documents are required:

✔ Sponsor letter✔ Sponsor bank statement✔ Copy of sponsor’s ID

Together, these make the family account acceptable.

6️⃣ Does Depositing Money at the Last Minute Cause Problems?

Yes. Large, sudden deposits are viewed as unreliable.

Embassy concerns:

• Source of funds unclear• Looks like last-minute preparation rather than genuine savings

Correct method:

✔ Funds should already be in the account beforehand✔ Balance should appear stable and consistent

7️⃣ Is a Euro Account Mandatory?

No. TL or any currency is acceptable.

The embassy examines:

• Euro equivalent of total balance• Transaction pattern• Clarity of sponsor support (if any)

Currency is not important, transparency is.

8️⃣ Is a Bank Letter Required?

Some embassy officers request it.

A bank letter usually includes:

• Account holder name• Total balance• Type of account• Latest updated date• Bank stamp and signature

Not mandatory, but strengthens the application.

9️⃣ Most Common Financial Mistakes

• Depositing money last minute• Presenting an empty account with no activity• Submitting a family account without a sponsor letter• Choosing the wrong insurance coverage• Not submitting grant documents• Providing screenshots instead of signed statements• Missing pages in the bank statement

These may lead to refusal or additional processing.

🎯 Summary

If financial sufficiency is shown correctly, the Romanian student visa process goes smoothly.A proper bank statement, consistent account history and a complete sponsor letter (if needed) strengthen the application significantly.

Key points:

• Sufficient minimum balance must be available• Statement must be signed and stamped• Sponsor letter must be complete (if applicable)• Grant letter must be included• Money flow must appear logical and stable

Meeting these conditions makes the financial section of the Romanian student visa much easier to pass.

html:
Intercity transportation in Romania is affordable and diverse.

Erasmus students mainly need information about travel options, reliable ticket platforms and route planning.

This guide explains all transportation methods in detail for students living in Romania.

1️⃣ How to Travel Between Cities in Romania?

Most common options:

🚆 Train🚌 Bus🚐 Minibus, microbus🚗 BlaBlaCar✈️ Airplane (for long distances)

Each has pros and cons below.

2️⃣ Train • Romania’s Most Used Transportation Method

Train travel is very common because many cities are connected by railway.

🎫 Where to buy train tickets?👉 mersultrenurilor.info

Advantages:

✅ Wide route network✅ Affordable price✅ No baggage limit✅ Fast train options (InterRegio)

Disadvantages:

⚠️ Slow trains in some regions⚠️ Possible delays⚠️ Old models on some lines

Still, trains are the most logical option for students.

3️⃣ Bus & Minibus • The Most Flexible System

Bus transportation is as common as trains and often faster.

🎫 Where to buy tickets?👉 autogari.ro

Advantages:

✅ Reaches places without train access✅ Faster on some routes✅ Student-friendly prices

Disadvantages:

⚠️ Less systematic than trains⚠️ Departure times may change⚠️ Possible baggage fees

4️⃣ BlaBlaCar • The Most Popular Alternative

BlaBlaCar is extremely common in Romania.

Why do people prefer it?

🚗 Fast travel💰 Affordable🗺️ Flexible routes✨ Clean vehicles

Advantages:

✅ Comfort of a personal car✅ Flexible schedule✅ Route variety

Disadvantages:

⚠️ No seats during busy hours⚠️ Drivers may cancel⚠️ Limited baggage space

Very popular and safe among students.

5️⃣ Plane • Fastest for Long Distances

Cities like Bucharest, Cluj-Napoca, Iași and Timișoara have international airports.

Advantages:

✈️ Extremely fast travel💰 Seasonal cheap tickets

Disadvantages:

⚠️ Extra city transportation cost⚠️ Limited flight options

6️⃣ Most Popular Routes in Romania

📍 Bucharest → Cluj-Napoca📍 Bucharest → Iași📍 Cluj-Napoca → Timișoara📍 Sibiu → Cluj📍 Brașov → Bucharest

All accessible by train, bus or BlaBlaCar.

7️⃣ What Affects Transportation Prices?

Prices change depending on:

📏 Distance🚆 Train type / bus company📅 Weekday or weekend⏳ Early booking🎓 Student discount

8️⃣ Best Option for Students

Short distance → 🚆 Train or 🚌 BusMedium distance → 🚆 Train or 🚗 BlaBlaCarLong distance → 🚆 Fast train or ✈️ Plane

9️⃣ Most Common Mistakes

🚫 Going to the wrong station🚫 Traveling without reservation🚫 Forgetting baggage fees🚫 Taking night trains without a couchette🚫 Not checking BlaBlaCar driver reviews

🎯 Summary

Romania offers wide and affordable transportation options.Choosing correctly between trains, buses, BlaBlaCar and planes makes travel fast and economical.Perfect for Erasmus students.

html:
The Erasmus Turna Portal is a platform that simplifies the application process for Erasmus+ programs for students in Türkiye. This portal allows students to apply for education, internships, or volunteer opportunities in different countries within the Erasmus+ program. You can also track your applications and receive updates on the process through this portal.

Features of Erasmus Turna Portal:

  1. Application Management : Students can apply for Erasmus+ through the portal, upload the required documents and track their application status.

  2. Information and Resources : The portal contains comprehensive information about Erasmus+ programmes, guides, and answers to frequently asked questions. This allows students to find all the information they need during the application process in one place.

  3. Progress Tracking : Students can see the status of their applications, check whether the required documents have been submitted, and complete missing documents.

  4. Support and Communication : The portal also provides a communication channel where students can receive support for any issues they encounter. This allows students to receive assistance with any difficulties they encounter during the application process.

  5. Management of Personal Information : Students can update their personal information on the portal and keep all contact information related to the application process under control.

Use of the Portal:

  • Register : To use the portal, students must first register and create a user account.

  • Applying : Once an account is created, students can start the application process by selecting the universities and programs they want to apply to for the Erasmus+ program.

  • Uploading Documents : Application documents can be uploaded through the portal. These documents typically include motivation letters, reference letters, and transcripts.

  • Status Updates : Students will be notified via the portal of any developments in the application process. This allows them to track the status of their application in real time.

The Erasmus Turna Portal is a valuable tool that helps Erasmus+ candidates in Türkiye manage their application process more streamlined and transparently. This portal saves students time and allows them to manage their applications more effectively.

html:
Universitaly is the official portal and platform for international and Italian students wishing to apply to higher education institutions in Italy. This platform is designed to simplify the application process for universities, master's programs, doctoral programs, and other educational programs in Italy.

Features of Universitaly:

  1. Application Process :

    • Application Management : Applications to universities and programs in Italy can be submitted through Universitaly. Students can upload the required documents for their chosen programs and track their applications.

    • Educational Institutions in Italy : The platform provides detailed information about all universities and higher education institutions in Italy. Students can review this information and choose the program that best suits them.

  2. Education and Career Guidance :

    • Program Information : Universitaly offers detailed information on all undergraduate, graduate, doctoral, and other study programs offered at universities in Italy. This helps students evaluate which program is best for them.

    • Career Opportunities : The platform also provides information about post-graduation career opportunities and the job market. This guides students on what to expect after graduation.

  3. Grammar :

    • Language Courses : Universitaly also offers information on Italian language courses for international students who want to study in Italy. These courses help students improve their Italian language skills and adapt to daily life in Italy.

    • Language Proficiency Exams : Information about the language proficiency exams required for students who want to study in Italy is also available on the portal.

  4. Visa and Residence Permit :

    • Visa Application Process : Universitaly provides detailed information about the visa application process for international students wishing to study in Italy. Students can learn more about what documents are required and how the application process works.

    • Residence Permit : A residence permit is required to study in Italy, and Universitaly provides guidance on how to obtain one.

  5. Registration and Admission Conditions :

    • Pre-registration and Admission : Provides information about the pre-registration process and requirements for admission to universities in Italy. This makes it easier to understand the steps involved in the application process.

    • Academic Requirements : Information is also provided about the academic documents, exams and other requirements required to apply to the university.

  6. Life Information :

    • Accommodation : Provides students with information about accommodation options, dormitories, student houses and other accommodation opportunities in Italy.

    • Daily Life : Provides guidance on daily life in Italy, including transportation, healthcare, and other practical information.

How to Use Universitaly:

  • Account Creation : To use the platform, you must first create an account. Once created, students can begin the application process.

  • Completing the Application Forms : Students fill out the necessary forms and upload the requested documents when applying to the programs they choose.

  • Application Tracking : Developments and changes occurring during the application process can be followed through the student's account.

Universitaly is a vital resource for students looking to study in Italy. This platform helps students manage the application process, choose the right program, and prepare for their studies in Italy.

html:
Spain offers a variety of scholarship programs for international and Spanish students with financial constraints. These scholarships are offered to help students cover the costs of their education. Funded by both government and private institutions, these scholarships are specifically designed for students experiencing financial hardship.

Scholarship Programs in Spain:

1. MEFP Scholarships (Ministerio de Educación y Formación Profesional) :

  • General Information : These scholarships, offered by the Spanish Ministry of Education and Vocational Training, are available to both Spanish and international students. They aim to support students with limited financial means.

  • Scholarship Types :

    • General Scholarships : General scholarships to cover students' educational expenses.

    • Tuition Fee Scholarships : Scholarships that help pay for university fees.

    • Relocation and Transportation Scholarships : Scholarships that cover transportation and moving expenses for students studying away from their place of residence.

  • Application Requirements : Depending on family income, students are required to submit documentation demonstrating their financial situation. Additionally, students' academic achievement is also considered.

2. Becas de Excelencia de la Comunidad de Madrid :

  • General Information : These scholarships, offered by the Community of Madrid, are available to both Spanish and international students. They are awarded specifically to students with high academic achievement but limited financial means.

  • Application Requirements : A certain level of academic achievement is required to apply for a scholarship. Additionally, students' financial situation and family income are also taken into consideration.

3. Erasmus+ Program :

  • General Information : The Erasmus+ program is a scholarship program funded by the European Union that provides students with the opportunity to study at various universities in Europe. It is open to both Spanish and international students.

  • Scholarship Types :

    • Student Mobility : Scholarships that allow students to study in another European country for a certain period of time.

    • Internship Mobility : Scholarships that allow students to do internships abroad.

  • Application Requirements : Erasmus+ scholarships are awarded based on academic achievement and financial standing. Students must also meet the requirements of their chosen program.

4. Becas MAEC-AECID :

html:
DSU (Diritto allo Studio Universitario) scholarships are a scholarship program for international and Italian students in Italy who are financially disadvantaged. DSU scholarships are provided to help students cover the cost of their education and are administered regionally. These scholarships offer a variety of financial assistance options, including tuition waivers, accommodation support, meal assistance, and financial support for books and other educational materials.

Key Features of DSU Scholarships:

  1. Scope of the Scholarship :

    • Tuition Fee Exemption : Students who win the scholarship may be exempt from university tuition fees.

    • Accommodation Support : Students can benefit from free or discounted accommodation in university dormitories.

    • Meal Assistance : Free or discounted meals are provided in university cafeterias.

    • Educational Material Support : Financial support may be provided for books, educational materials and other academic needs.

    • Scholarship Payment : The scholarship amount varies depending on the student's financial situation, academic achievement, and the decision of the regional DSU office. Scholarship payments are generally made in two installments.

  2. Application Conditions :

    • Financial Status : The applicant's family income must be below a certain threshold. Income and assets are proven through the ISEE (Indicatore della Situazione Economica Equivalente).

    • Academic Performance : Students are required to maintain a certain level of academic achievement. This level of achievement may vary by university and department.

    • Citizenship and Residency : International students studying in Italy are also eligible to apply for DSU scholarships. However, they may be required to have regular residence in Italy.

    • Student Status : Scholarships are generally available to full-time students. Different conditions may apply to part-time students.

  3. Application Process :

    • Regional Administration : DSU scholarships are administered regionally in Italy. Therefore, scholarship applications should be submitted to the DSU office in the region where the student studies or resides.

    • Application Deadlines : The application process usually begins in the summer months, and students must complete the relevant documents and submit them by the application deadline.

    • Required Documents : The following documents are generally required for the application: İSEE document, academic transcript, ID and residence permit (for foreign students), documents showing family income and assets.

    • Announcement of Results : Application results are generally announced at the beginning of the academic year. Students who have won a scholarship are informed of the scholarship amount and terms and conditions.

  4. Continuity of Scholarship :

    • Academic Performance : Maintaining academic success is essential for the scholarship to continue. A certain number of credits may be required and satisfactory exam performance may be required.

    • Change in Income Situation : If there is a significant change in the income situation of the student or their family, the scholarship may be re-evaluated and this may affect the scholarship amount.

  5. Additional Benefits and Supports :

    • Study Abroad Support : Some DSU scholarships also provide support to students participating in study abroad programs such as Erasmus.

    • Additional Aid : Additional aid may be provided to students who are in a much worse financial situation or additional scholarships may be provided for special circumstances.

DSU Scholarship Benefits:

  • Accessibility : DSU scholarships cater to a wide range of financially disadvantaged students and provide equal educational opportunities.

  • Various Supports : Helps students go through the learning process more comfortably by greatly reducing their education costs.

  • Regional Support : Administering scholarships regionally ensures that students receive support based on needs in their area.

DSU scholarships also offer a great opportunity for international students looking to study in Italy. Taking advantage of these scholarships can significantly reduce the cost of studying in Italy and help students achieve their academic goals.

Germany offers various scholarships to international and German students to support those with financial constraints. These scholarships are specifically designed for students experiencing financial hardship and offer financial support in a variety of areas, from tuition fees to living expenses. Scholarships in Germany are typically provided by government agencies, private foundations, universities, and non-governmental organizations.

Scholarship Programs in Germany:

1. DAAD Scholarships (Deutscher Akademischer Austauschdienst - German Academic Exchange Service) :

  • General Information : DAAD is one of Germany's largest scholarship providers. It offers a wide range of scholarships for both German and international students.

  • Scholarship Types :

    • Postgraduate Scholarships : Scholarships for students pursuing master's and doctoral degrees. These scholarships are typically fully comprehensive and cover expenses such as tuition fees, living expenses, and health insurance.

    • Research Scholarships : Scholarships awarded for doctoral and postdoctoral research projects.

    • Short-Term Scholarships : Scholarships awarded for language courses, summer schools and short-term research projects.

  • Application Requirements : Applications for DAAD scholarships are evaluated based on criteria such as academic achievement, motivation letter, reference letters, and proposed research project. Additionally, some scholarships require proof of a specific language proficiency (usually English or German).

2. Deutschlandstipendium :

  • General Information : This scholarship program is jointly funded by the German government and the private sector. Available to both German and international students, it provides financial support as well as a variety of career development and mentoring opportunities.

  • Scholarship Scope : Students who win a scholarship receive a monthly stipend of €300. This scholarship helps students cover their education and daily living expenses.

  • Application Requirements : During the application process, students' academic achievement, social responsibility, and personal development are evaluated. Furthermore, students' financial situation and needs are also taken into consideration.

3. Friedrich Ebert Stiftung Scholarships :

  • General Information : The Friedrich Ebert Foundation is a foundation that offers scholarships to promote social justice and democratic values. It specifically awards scholarships to socially disadvantaged students who demonstrate academic achievement.

  • Scholarship Types :

    • Undergraduate and Postgraduate Scholarships : Scholarships for international students pursuing undergraduate and graduate studies in Germany. These scholarships cover tuition fees, living expenses, and study materials.

    • PhD Scholarships : Scholarships for students who want to pursue a PhD in Germany.

  • Application Requirements : Academic achievement, social responsibility, and political and community involvement are considered. Documentation demonstrating applicants' financial situation is also required.

4. Konrad Adenauer Stiftung Scholarships :

  • General Information : The Konrad Adenauer Foundation offers scholarships to students studying in fields such as politics, law, economics, and social sciences. These scholarships are available to both German and international students.

  • Scholarship Types :

    • Postgraduate Scholarships : Scholarships for students enrolled in master's and doctoral programs.

    • Research Grants : Grants awarded for academic research projects.

  • Application Requirements : Applicants are evaluated not only on their academic achievement but also on their social and political involvement. Students are also required to provide documentation of their financial situation.

5. Heinrich Böll Stiftung Scholarships :

  • General Information : The Heinrich Böll Foundation offers scholarships to students pursuing studies on the environment, human rights, democracy, and sustainable development. These scholarships are available to both international and German students.

  • Scholarship Types :

    • Postgraduate Scholarships : Scholarships for students enrolled in master's and doctoral programs.

    • Research Grants : Grants awarded for academic research projects.

  • Application Requirements : Criteria such as academic achievement, social responsibility, and interest and participation in environmental and sustainability issues are evaluated. Additionally, the applicant's financial situation and needs are taken into consideration.

Application Process for Scholarships in Germany:

  1. Review the Application Requirements : To decide which scholarship is right for you, it is important to carefully review the application requirements and scholarship scope.

  2. Preparation of Required Documents :

    • Academic Transcripts : Documents showing your educational history.

    • Financial Status Documents : Documents showing your family income status and financial needs.

    • Motivation Letter : A letter explaining why you want the scholarship and your academic/personal goals.

    • Language Certificates : English or German language proficiency is required for some scholarships.

  3. Applying : Applications for most scholarship programs are accepted online. You must complete the application form and upload the required documents on the scholarship provider's websites.

  4. Waiting for Results : Scholarship applications can typically take several months to be processed. Once the results are announced, students who have been awarded a scholarship will be informed about the scholarship amount and terms.

These scholarship programs in Germany provide significant support, especially to students with limited financial means. These scholarships provide students with the opportunity to receive a quality education in Germany and significantly reduce their educational expenses.
